<security_assessment>

<details>
The PKGBUILD contains no command substitutions, dynamic code execution, or suspicious top-level commands. The source array references a single .deb file from the project's own GitHub releases (https://github.com/mayocream/koharu), which is a standard upstream source. The sha256sum is provided and not set to SKIP. There is no pkgver() function defined. The `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` command will only fetch and verify the source archive without executing any code from the package itself, and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` merely parses the PKGBUILD variables. No malicious behavior occurs during these specific commands.
</details>
<evidence>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The .SRCINFO file is a standard Arch Linux packaging metadata file for the koharu-bin package. It declares a single source: a prebuilt Debian package downloaded from the project's own GitHub releases (https://github.com/mayocream/koharu/releases/download/0.79.4/koharu_0.79.4_amd64.deb), with a valid SHA-256 checksum provided (not skipped). The dependencies are standard system libraries (gtk3, gdk-pixbuf2, glib2, fontconfig, openssl, gcc-libs) and optional components for local AI features. There is no obfuscated code, no data exfiltration, no execution of untrusted remote content, no backdoors, and no modification of unrelated system files. The file is consistent with ordinary AUR binary packaging practices.
</details>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is a standard Arch Linux AUR package for distributing a pre-built binary from GitHub releases. It downloads the official `.deb` release from `https://github.com/mayocream/koharu/releases/download/${pkgver}/koharu_${pkgver}_amd64.deb` and uses `bsdtar` to extract its contents into the package directory. The SHA256 checksum is properly provided and matches the downloaded binary. No suspicious network destinations, obfuscated code, or unexpected system modifications are present. The package dependencies (gtk3, gdk-pixbuf2, glib2, fontconfig, openssl, gcc-libs) are appropriate for a GUI application. This follows standard AUR `-bin` package practices for distributing upstream pre-built binaries.
</details>
